title: Align SendMessage tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all SendMessage improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Current TS baseline is ../src/tools/SendMessageTool/SendMessageTool.ts plus registration in ../src/tools.ts. Per tools/reports/SendMessage.md, the removed bridge/Remote Control delivery path is treated as out of scope for Go parity; this report therefore focuses on teammate mailbox, local agent continuation, UDS, and structured control messages. The Go implementation has useful coverage for those paths, including mailbox writes, UDS, local-agent resume, request-id generation, and shutdown approval cancellation. Remaining parity gaps are concentrated in sender identity spoofing, loose input/schema and lifecycle metadata, Go-only MessageBus fallback/output, mailbox state/layout/read semantics, broadcast behavior, structured control payload/lifecycle details, permission/read-only handling, and stale alignment tests that assert non-current TS envelope behavior. Verification note: attempted `go test ./tools ./swarm ./permissions -run 'TestSendMessage|TestRequiresBridgePermission|TestIsMailboxRetryable|TestModeAllowAllSendMessage|TestCacheKeyDifferentiatesSendMessageTargets' -count=1`; `./swarm` had no matching tests and passed, while `./tools` and `./permissions` could not build because provider/responses.go references undefined classifyResponsesAPIError.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go lets tool input spoof sender identity and authority
improvement_points.description: TS SendMessage input only accepts to, summary, and message; sender identity is derived from runtime/team state. Go's SendMessageInput adds from and content, then trusts from for mailbox sender selection, MessageBus reply routing, and structured plan-approval authority checks. A model/tool caller can therefore claim to be team-lead or another teammate in Go in ways the TS tool contract does not permit.

improvement_points.title: Go model-visible schema, description, availability, and read-only metadata are looser than TS
improvement_points.description: TS publishes a specific tool description, prompt, zod union for three structured message types, summary requirement for plain text except UDS, shouldDefer/searchHint, isEnabled via agent-swarms, and isReadOnly for string messages. Go publishes a broad object message schema, omits UDS/bridge from the visible to description despite supporting uds routing, exposes content/from as typed inputs, registers SendMessage unconditionally, and has no SendMessage-specific read-only hook in the tool interface.

improvement_points.title: Go falls back to a coordinator MessageBus/envelope path that TS SendMessage does not expose
improvement_points.description: For plain non-UDS messages, TS routes to local-agent continuation first and then mailbox write/broadcast. If no explicit teamName is available for a direct message, writeToMailbox defaults to the default team inbox. Go only uses mailbox routing when loadActiveTeamConfig returns a config; otherwise it routes through coordinator.MessageBus and returns an Envelope with request_id/kind/delivered/recipients/reply_text/quorum. Existing Go tests pin this Go-only path using content/from inputs.

improvement_points.title: Mailbox file layout, read lifecycle, and routing metadata are not TS-compatible
improvement_points.description: TS mailbox messages are stored under a team-level inboxes directory, include a read boolean, preserve messages while marking them read, and SendMessage routing returns senderColor/targetColor when available. Go stores each recipient under {team}/{agent}/inbox.json, has no read field, reads by removing/clearing the inbox file, and SendMessage writes do not populate Color or return senderColor/targetColor even though TeamMember has a Color field.

improvement_points.title: Broadcast validation, recipient selection, failure semantics, and output differ
improvement_points.description: TS broadcast requires an active team context and team file, broadcasts to every team file member except the sender regardless of isActive, and returns success true with message 'Message broadcast to N teammate(s): ...'. Go falls back to MessageBus broadcast when no team config is loaded, filters inactive persisted members, returns delivered/failed bookkeeping for mailbox broadcast, and uses a different message format.

improvement_points.title: Structured control message payloads and lifecycle side effects are incomplete or over-broad
improvement_points.description: TS SendMessage accepts only shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response structured inputs. Its plan approval response includes inherited permissionMode, plan rejection writes default feedback when none is supplied, shutdown approval includes pane/backend metadata when known, and non-in-process approval schedules gracefulShutdown. Go accepts extra structured message types on its no-team MessageBus path, misses permissionMode/default feedback in mailbox payloads, omits paneId/backendType from shutdown approval payloads, and marks members inactive/aborts local background sessions instead of matching TS graceful process-exit behavior.

improvement_points.title: Permission/read-only handling and supported error semantics do not match TS
improvement_points.description: For the supported non-bridge subset, TS marks plain string SendMessage calls read-only and structured messages non-read-only. Go classifies all SendMessage calls as medium risk through the generic permission system. For bridge, which is excluded from this report's candidate scope, Go currently implements only an Execute-time grant registry and tests that a granted bridge target falls through to no-transport behavior; this is not equivalent to TS checkPermissions if bridge is ever reintroduced.

improvement_points.title: Go alignment tests partly encode stale/nonexistent TS contracts and miss current TS parity cases
improvement_points.description: Several SendMessage alignment tests reference TS files that are not present in the current ../src/tools/SendMessageTool directory and assert an envelope/InflightTable contract that the current TS SendMessageTool.ts does not expose. At the same time, tests do not cover sender spoofing rejection, TS mailbox layout/read flags/colors, current TS direct/broadcast output shapes, plan approval permissionMode/default feedback, or TS isReadOnly behavior. Targeted Go verification is currently also blocked by an unrelated provider build error.

implementation_subtasks.title: Remove or ignore Go-only SendMessage from/content inputs for user-facing calls
acceptance_criteria: User-facing SendMessage derives sender from runtime/team/env context only; input from cannot spoof team-lead or another teammate.
TS-compatible calls require message for user-facing SendMessage; content is either removed, ignored, or moved behind an internal-only compatibility path with explicit tests.
Pending-reply drain behavior no longer depends on caller-supplied from in the TS-compatible SendMessage path.
Regression tests show from=team-lead cannot authorize plan_approval_response unless runtime context is actually team lead.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align SendMessage schema, description, availability, and read-only metadata with TS
acceptance_criteria: Published Name and Description match TS: SendMessage / 'Send a message to another agent'.
Published schema documents teammate, '*', and supported UDS targets; structured message objects are constrained to TS SendMessage's three structured types.
SendMessage visibility follows TS isAgentSwarmsEnabled-equivalent gating in normal tool assembly, while preserving any intentional coordinator/simple-mode exception with explicit tests.
Plain string messages are represented as read-only in the Go permission/risk layer; structured messages are not.
Unsupported bridge delivery remains explicitly out of scope unless a separate bridge transport parity task is created.

implementation_subtasks.title: Replace or isolate the Go-only MessageBus fallback from the TS-compatible SendMessage path
acceptance_criteria: TS-compatible direct SendMessage without an active team config follows TS mailbox/default-team behavior or returns the same validation/error semantics TS would expose; it does not silently switch to Envelope output.
If MessageBus send/await remains needed for Go internals, it is moved behind a clearly internal transport or separate tool path and no longer changes the public SendMessage contract.
Direct SendMessage output in the public path is {success,message,routing?}, not Envelope.
Tests distinguish TS-compatible SendMessage from any internal MessageBus transport.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align mailbox persistence, read lifecycle, and routing color metadata
acceptance_criteria: Mailbox write/read format is compatible with TS TeammateMessage, including read:false on write and optional color/summary fields.
Inbox path/layout is TS-compatible or a tested compatibility adapter reads/writes both Go and TS layouts without losing messages.
Mailbox read lifecycle preserves read/audit semantics equivalent to TS markMessagesAsRead; destructive read/remove behavior is not used for the TS-compatible path unless explicitly isolated.
Direct SendMessage routing includes senderColor and targetColor when available from team state/config.
Tests assert file layout, read flag behavior, color round-trip, and direct routing color fields.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align broadcast validation, recipients, failure semantics, and output
acceptance_criteria: Broadcast without active team context returns the TS-style 'Not in a team context...' failure instead of MessageBus envelope output.
Broadcast to a missing team returns the TS-style Team does not exist failure.
Recipient selection matches TS: every team file member except sender by case-insensitive name; no extra IsActive filter in the TS-compatible path.
Successful broadcast output matches TS success/message/recipients/routing shape and message wording.
If Go keeps partial-success bookkeeping, it is isolated from the TS-compatible output path or documented as non-parity internal behavior with tests.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align structured SendMessage control payloads and shutdown/plan lifecycle effects
acceptance_criteria: Structured SendMessage user-facing input accepts only shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response, matching TS.
Plan approval is authorized from real team-lead runtime state, not input from.
Approved plan payload includes permissionMode with TS plan-mode default handling.
Rejected plan payload includes feedback, defaulting to 'Plan needs revision' when omitted.
Shutdown approval payload includes paneId/backendType when known.
Approved shutdown lifecycle matches TS for in-process and non-in-process equivalents, including actual session/process termination semantics or a documented Go-equivalent with tests.

implementation_subtasks.title: Refresh SendMessage parity tests against the current TS baseline
acceptance_criteria: Alignment tests reference only files and behavior present in the current TS baseline: ../src/tools.ts, ../src/tools/SendMessageTool/SendMessageTool.ts, prompt.ts, constants.ts, teammateMailbox.ts, peerAddress.ts, LocalAgentTask, and resumeAgent.
Tests stop asserting nonexistent Envelope.ts/types.ts/structured.ts/leader_inbox.ts/SendAndAwait.ts contracts as TS SendMessage parity.

New red/green tests cover sender spoofing, strict input surface, no-team direct message behavior, direct output/routing colors, mailbox read flags/layout, broadcast output, plan approval permissionMode/default feedback, shutdown pane/backend metadata, and plain-message read-only classification.
Test package build blockers unrelated to SendMessage are either resolved upstream or documented so SendMessage verification can run deterministically.
SendMessage input validation and schema behavior match the original TS implementation for all report gaps.
SendMessage model-visible output and structured result data match TS golden fixtures.
SendMessage runtime side effects, state transitions, permission decisions, and error branches listed in improvement_points are implemented or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
